crossCuttingObservations: Access failure is the main churn engine: 11 cancellation posts are explicitly framed as 'I can't use what I pay for', and separate clusters exist for members who cannot even log in far enough to reach the cancel screen. A Navigator that fixes access would deflect a large share of billing-cancel volume.

Self-serve billing controls appear undiscoverable. 'Where do I cancel?' (17 items, 2022-2025) and 'Where do I change my card?' (12 items, 2023-2026) recur unchanged across four years, with 5 and 6 items respectively receiving zero replies.

Non-response is itself a complaint. Roughly a third of all items have commentCount 0, and multiple verbatims say the member wrote three times, messaged Alice/Chas hours ago, or contacted support with no answer - this appears inside billing, login and email clusters alike.

Cancellation requests are posted publicly in community spaces rather than sent through a billing flow, and often include personal data (full names, email addresses). There is no evidence in the corpus that a public post results in an actioned cancellation.

The Discord identity-matching verification flow produced a dense burst of near-identical questions on 24-27 July 2023 (name-match, please-verify-me, verify errors, claim-account). The same pattern re-fires after any logout, device change or platform rename.

A distinct September-October 2024 wave concerns Discord platform-level suspensions attributed to the Patriot Talk server - a vendor-side action the community cannot resolve, needing a different answer from ordinary access loss.

Platform churn on the community's side (Talk Time renamed Patriot Talk, Discord to Telegram/Signal/Campfire, Rumble/Twitch/TubePatriot/Roku for streams) resets member knowledge each time and regenerates the same access and 'where do I watch' clusters.

Show schedule and replay location questions (20 and 12 items) are asked daily-scale and are structurally answerable by a published schedule plus a replay index; one member explicitly requested shows be listed on Events with watch links.

The membership self-describes as older and non-technical ('I'm 75', 'old ladies like me', 'not computor geek', 'elderly and disabled'), and asks are frequently for step-by-step walkthroughs or for an admin to perform the action, not for a link.

Distinguish three billing answers that members phrase identically: how to cancel (self-serve steps), cancellation not actioned / still charged (escalation and dispute path), and refund (policy). Roughly a quarter of cancel-themed items fall outside the plain how-to answer.

crossCuttingObservations: Navigation questions dominate this chunk and cluster around three destinations: state/county groups (27 items), Patriot Talk/Talk Time (14 items plus 5 more about its setup instructions), and the QFS/Humanitarian rooms. All three are 'where is X' questions that a single Navigator answer with a direct deep link would resolve.

Platform redesigns are a recurring trigger: menu items disappearing, the TV icon vanishing, 'Patriot Talk moved', 'various page just removed', and notifications pages breaking 'since they loaded that new crap' all spike right after changes. A change-log / 'what moved where' answer would absorb a large share of these.

The single biggest notification cluster is 'settings are on but nothing arrives' (22 items, 11 with no reply at all) and it is concentrated in the Quantum Financial Room during 2022 test-notification pushes. It needs a different answer from 'how do I turn notifications on' (10 items) and from 'emails specifically aren't arriving' (6 items).

A high share of items go completely unanswered — roughly a third across this chunk, and worse in some clusters (redirect problems 4/6, room-finding 4/6, delete-own-content 3/3). Several members explicitly note that nobody replied, which is the main churn signal here rather than billing.

Members conflate the app and the website: many problems reported as 'the site is broken' are Mighty Networks app issues where the peer-suggested workaround is 'use patriotchute.com in a browser'. The Navigator should ask app-vs-browser first for any 'can't see posts / can't post / crashes' report.

A distinct self-described 'non-technical / older member' voice runs through the corpus ('techno tortoise', 'I'll be 75', 'tech challenged', 'lost in the apple sauce'). Answers that depend on multi-page written instructions (Patriot Talk/Discord setup) are visibly failing this segment — the instructions themselves generate support volume.

Emotional escalation is strongest around moderation and missing content ('who can remove a simple post', 'is this censorship', 'the mods remove all of my posts') and around privacy ('I am getting EVERYONE'S personal messages'). These need careful, separate answers rather than generic navigation help.

Several 'find' questions are really about the humanitarian project workflow: where the template is (7), where to upload it (12), how to find your own submission afterwards (4), and never hearing back after submitting. Treating these as one workflow FAQ rather than isolated navigation items would cover ~25 items.

crossCuttingObservations: Access to third-party platforms (Discord/Talk Time, Telegram, Signal, Rumble, Zoom) generates the largest share of questions in this chunk — roughly a third of all clustered items — and carries nearly all of the churn-risk language, because members equate failure on those services with the membership they pay for here.

The same questions recur unchanged across the entire 2021-2026 window: 'how do I get into Talk Time' appears in 2022, 2023, 2025 and 2026; 'how do I join my state group' spans 2023 to 2025. There is no durable answer surface, so each member re-asks from scratch.

Unanswered rate is highest exactly where onboarding fails: 7 of 9 'join my state group' posts, 5 of 7 'where is the replay' posts, 4 of 5 'where is the Discord invite' posts, and 5 of 12 'where do I start' posts have zero replies.
Questions asked inside comment threads (rather than as top-level posts) almost never show a recorded reply, so members who ask in-thread are the least likely to get help.

Churn risk concentrates where loss of access meets billing: being banned by Discord while still being charged, paying for a trial month and never getting a working invite, Telegram-only content for members who refuse Telegram, and repeated unanswered requests to join a state group.

State groups follow a visible lifecycle in the questions: join -> who is our director/coordinator -> is anything happening here -> this group is dead. 'Who is our state coordinator' (14 items) and 'my group is inactive' (5 items) are the two biggest state-level themes, and volunteer offers to lead a county frequently go unanswered.

Many members self-identify as non-technical or elderly ('not an avid computer savvy person', 'I've never used anything like this', 'watching a replay for dummies') and explicitly ask for step-by-step instructions or a tutorial rather than a link.
Members frequently repost the same question in both their state space and HOME | Members Lobby, inflating volume and splitting any answer that does arrive.

A distinct free-speech grievance pattern runs through moderation questions: members who are muted, blocked, or removed frame it as censorship on a platform sold as censorship-free, and several escalate to threats to cancel or sue.

Navigation questions cluster around things that moved or vanished (Talk Time gone from the menu, Discovery missing, rooms and posts deleted), suggesting platform changes ship without an in-product changelog members can find.
